newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HISTORY FAVOURS SPURS IN CUP DUELS WITH UNITED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HISTORY FAVOURS SPURS IN CUP DUELS WITH UNITED.

text.p: No clubs have had more success in the history of the English F.A. Cup than Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur who clash in the third round at Old Trafford on Sunday.

When United beat Liverpool to win the Cup for the ninth time last May, they broke the record for the number of victories that Tottenham had set when they won the Cup for the eighth time in 1991. Manchester United had equalled that record when they beat Chelsea in 1994.

In the 21 seasons since 1976 the two clubs have reached the cup final 13 times between them with United winning the trophy six times (1977, 1983, 1985, 1990, 1994, 1996) and Spurs three (1981, 1982 and 1991).
The two sides have never met in the final but Sunday's match will be almost as important as the Cup final itself for Tottenham.
Already out of the hunt for the title and out of the League Cup, Tottenham's season will effectively be over if they lose to United on Sunday.
But while Tottenham go to Old Trafford shell-shocked from their 7-1 drubbing at Newcastle last weekend, they also have the omens on their side.
Sunday's meeting will be the 13th time United and Spurs have met in the Cup. Of the previous 12 games, Spurs have won five, United two and five matches have been drawn.
United knocked Tottenham out of the Cup twice, in 1926 and 1979, while Spurs knocked out United in 1899, 1923, 1962 in the semifinal, 1968 and 1980.

That tie in 1980 was one of the most dramatic matches in the long history between the sides. The previous season United had knocked Spurs out after a quarter-final replay at Old Trafford, and earlier in the 1979-80 season they had played two blood-and- guts matches in the League Cup which United had taken 4-3 on aggregate.
So after drawing 1-1 at White Hart Lane in the third round, the teams were ready for their sixth cup battle in less than a year at Old Trafford four days later.

United seemed set for victory after Tottenham's goalkeeper Milija Aleksic was carried off halfway through the game after suffering a head injury in a clash with United forward Joe Jordan. Glenn Hoddle went in goal for Tottenham, who bravely held out against United's rampant attacks throughout the second half and for half-an-hour of extra time.
Then, with the score still 0-0, a minute of extra time remaining and a second replay beckoning, Ossie Ardiles collected the ball at the edge of the United penalty area.
The little Argentinian chose his spot perfectly and looped the ball over United goalkeeper Gary Bailey to give Tottenham a dramatic 1-0 victory.

Spurs eventually went out in the quarter-finals to Liverpool but they won the Cup in 1981 and 1982 while United won it in 1983. Oddly all three of those finals went to replays with Spurs winning the 100th Cup Final in 1981 against Manchester City and the 1982 final against QPR while United needed two games before beating Brighton the following year.
Spurs do not have players of the calibre of Hoddle and Ardiles for this Sunday's clash, and on paper at least, seem to have little chance against the Cup holders.

But Spurs have a special affinity with the Cup and have history marginally on their side. That might not be enough to beat United but it could be enough to earn them a replay, which could provide another good omen as United have never beaten Spurs in the Cup at White Hart Lane.
